this recipe is written for a 14 to 16 lb turkey, so ours will finish sooner. Start checking the thigh temperature about 1 hour after lowering the oven to 350°F. It's done at 165°F, whatever the clock says.

blocks.content: The fastest practical and safe way to speed up thawing is the cold-water method. It works even if the turkey is already partially thawed in the refrigerator.

content.text: Keep the turkey in its original packaging, provided it is watertight. Otherwise, use a leakproof bag.
Completely submerge the turkey in cold tap water in a sink or large container.
Change the water every 30 minutes so it stays cold.
Allow about 30 minutes per pound for a fully frozen turkey. A partially thawed turkey takes less time.
Keep thawing the turkey in the refrigerator overnight.
Switch to the cold-water method early Thanksgiving morning.
Cook immediately once cold-water thawing is done.
Never use warm or hot water to speed up thawing.
Never thaw a turkey on the countertop.
A partially frozen turkey can safely be roasted in the oven, but it will need extra cooking time.
Never deep-fry a frozen or partially frozen turkey.
Make sure the turkey reaches 165°F in the thickest part of the breast, the innermost part of the thigh, and the innermost part of the wing.
